PUBLISHED: 2026-11-23T05:47:18+0000
Oil prices fell slightly on Monday as investors focused on ⁠Middle East oil flows, with persistent shipping and refinery attacks in the Middle East offering support.Brent crude futures ​fell 60 cents, ​or 0.65%, to $91.97 a ​barrel by 0844 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate futures were down 49 cents, or 0.59%, to $82.92 a barrel.

[Additional extracted content from same article via fetch tool:]
Last week, Brent declined 4% and WTI 5%.
PVM analyst Tamas Varga: "Oil recorded its third successive weekly loss, with pressure coming primarily from the supply side of the equation." "Iranian attacks on ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz are taking their toll."
UKMTO reported multiple attacks on shipping in the Gulf and near the Strait of Hormuz over the weekend. Bahrain said an Iranian attack hit a civilian industrial facility on Saturday. IRGC said they launched a missile-and-drone assault on US military positions in Bahrain, home to the US Navy's 5th Fleet.
On Sunday, the Iran-aligned Houthi movement said it attacked a Saudi Arabian oil refinery.
OPEC+ ministers will hold a series of meetings on November 29 to decide their 2027 output policy.
COP31 talks in Turkey collapsed on Sunday, the first such collapse since 2009.
